validity.researcher_notes: The line is real and correctly classified as a transmission gas trunk. Ukrtransgaz, Ukrainian Wikipedia and the Kursk regional government page name it. It is not a duplicate of P0775 plus P1460: they differ in diameter and the earlier geometry test failed. The sheet length of 771 km equals the VTG table's 619 km for the DN1400 line plus 152 km for a DN1200 line in the same block, so two lines appear to have been added together. Diameter 1420 is supported by the Kursk page; other sources say the nominal 1400. Capacity 95 million m3 per day is the figure for every DN1420 string in the Kursk bundle, which is high for one string, so treat it as a design figure.

fills.researcher_notes: No source dated 2024 or later was found that says this line is in use. The Kursk regional government page (archived December 2022) and the Gazprom Kursk compressor-station page (archived May 2025) both list the line, but only as part of the corridor's history. Russian transit through Ukraine stopped on 1 January 2025. Searched Russian and Ukrainian news, the Ukrainian operator site is blocked (HTTP 403).

Kursk regional government page gives 1420 mm for «Елец-Кривой Рог». Ukrainian Wikipedia and the VTG table say 1400, the nominal size. Both are the same pipe designation.

The VTG table (archived June 2022) lists «Елец-Кременчуг-Кривой Рог» at 619 km, DN1400, and a second DN1200 line of 152 km in the same block. 619 + 152 = 771, which is the sheet figure. The sheet looks like it summed two lines. Proposing 619 km. The 152 km line is not named in its own cell, so which pipe it is stays unclear. Spec concern filed.
